metadata.title: No Verification Path, No Delegation.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: which check actually matches which kind of Claude output? Lands the carry-out that no verification path means no delegation.
metadata.anchor_pair: B03 -> B08 (the fabricated-citation card: planted as a clean-reading fake that only 'open the source' catches; returned run through the matrix and logged as the reel closes)
metadata.one_flag: B07 - the matrix assumes the primary source is reachable; when it isn't, downgrade confidence instead of skipping the check

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes that if Claude's output reads clean, they've verified it. They haven't — only edited it. So which check actually fits a citation, a claim, or a number?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'If Claude's output reads clean, I've verified it — right?', hesitates on 'verified', corrects to 'edited'

props.text:
If Claude's output
reads clean, I've
verified it —
right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('verified' -> 'edited') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Claude can hand back a citation, a claim, and a quantified number in the same paragraph, in exactly the same confident voice. Fluent, assured prose is a training habit — it looks identical whether the content underneath is verified or invented.

shot.new_visual_element: a citation card, a claim card, a number card, all carrying the same confident 'voice' mark

production_viz.label: Same confident voice, three outputs
production_viz.mechanic: Three small pill cards in a row: CITATION, CLAIM, NUMBER. Each glows with an identical small 'confident voice' mark above it. Caption beneath: 'fluent either way'.

beats.narration_text: So the natural move is to proofread: read it over, check that it flows, catch typos and awkward phrasing. If it reads clean, it feels checked.

shot.new_visual_element: a passage, a red pen sweeping over it for style, a checkmark forming

production_viz.label: The natural guess
production_viz.mechanic: A block of text. A pen icon sweeps across it left to right, marking style tweaks. A confident checkmark forms beneath, captioned 'reads clean = checked?'.

beats.narration_text: Here's the case that breaks it. A fabricated citation — real journal name, right year, a plausible title, not one typo. Reading it start to finish catches nothing. Opening the actual source is the only step that shows it doesn't exist.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - the citation card, checkmark forming, then cracking open to 'SOURCE: NOT FOUND'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - a clean-reading fake
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A citation card: journal, year, title, all formatted correctly, not a single typo. A checkmark forms. Then the card cracks open like a shell to reveal terracotta text inside: 'SOURCE: NOT FOUND'. THIS EXACT CARD RETURNS AT B08.

beats.narration_text: Editing asks: is this clear, coherent, well organized? Auditing asks: is this true, traceable, and supported by the source? Two different questions — and editing never once opens the source.

shot.new_visual_element: two question cards, EDIT vs AUDIT; only the AUDIT arrow reaches a source document

production_viz.label: Edit asks, audit asks
production_viz.mechanic: Two cards side by side: EDIT — 'is this clear?'; AUDIT — 'is this true?'. An arrow from AUDIT reaches down to a small source-document icon; no arrow leaves EDIT. Caption beneath: 'editing never opens the source'.

beats.narration_text: The verification matrix assigns the right check before you read for clarity. A citation: open the source, confirm the title and author, confirm it says what's claimed. A number: recompute a sample, check the denominator. A claim: trace it to one specific sentence, not a vibe.

shot.new_visual_element: three-row matrix: CITATION -> open the source; NUMBER -> recompute + denominator; CLAIM -> trace to one sentence

production_viz.label: Every output type has its own check
production_viz.mechanic: A three-row table: CITATION -> 'OPEN THE SOURCE'; NUMBER -> 'RECOMPUTE + DENOMINATOR'; CLAIM -> 'TRACE TO ONE SENTENCE'. Caption beneath: 'assigned before you read for clarity'.

beats.narration_text: The depth of that check should match the consequence. Personal notes: light, just scan for obvious errors. An internal planning document: moderate, spot-check the figures. Anything published, submitted, or signed: strict, full audit before it leaves your hands. A client email is strict — the consequence is yours.

shot.new_visual_element: three gate tiers, LIGHT/MODERATE/STRICT, widening in weight; 'client email' slots into STRICT

production_viz.label: The gate matches the consequence
production_viz.mechanic: Three stacked bars widening downward: LIGHT (personal notes), MODERATE (internal doc), STRICT (published/signed). A small 'client email' card slides down and locks into the STRICT bar. Caption beneath: 'the consequence is yours'.

beats.narration_text: One flag: this only works if you can actually reach the primary source. Some claims sit behind paywalls or private data you can't open. Then the honest move is downgrading your confidence in that piece, not skipping the check and calling it verified anyway.

shot.new_visual_element: THE FLAG - a locked source card, a checklist step downgrading from 'VERIFIED' to 'UNCONFIRMED'

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG - can you reach the source?
production_viz.mechanic: A single terracotta FLAG marker over the beat, the reel's only hedge, labeled as one. A source card shown behind a lock icon. Beside it a status label reading 'VERIFIED' crosses out and is replaced by 'UNCONFIRMED' — downgraded, not skipped.

beats.narration_text: Run the fabricated citation back through the matrix: open the source — not found. That's a record, not a guess. But passing every check doesn't prove the whole output is airtight — it catches the known risks for that type, not everything. And failing one check doesn't mean the whole thing is garbage either — it means that one piece needs a closer look.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the citation card run through the matrix to 'SOURCE: NOT FOUND, logged'; two dimmed captions beneath

production_viz.label: The record, then both directions
production_viz.mechanic: THE B03 ANCHOR RETURNS: the same citation card, run through a small matrix icon into a log card reading 'SOURCE: NOT FOUND — logged'. Beneath, two dimmed captions fade in: 'ALL CHECKS PASSED != AIRTIGHT' and 'ONE FAILED CHECK != WRONG'.

beats.narration_text: No verification path, no delegation. That's not outsourcing labor — it's outsourcing judgment.

props.quote: No verification path, no delegation. That's not outsourcing labor — it's outsourcing judgment.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want to build a verification matrix for an agent that produces citations, claims, and quantified findings. For each output type, tell me the specific check I'd run, the evidence that check needs, and how I'd implement it as a concrete tool call before the output ships. Liam, in for Bear.
